cohort: Pregnant women with dichorionic twin pregnancies (n=189) or singleton pregnancies (n=567) and a BMI > 30, matched with non-obese controls
finding: Obesity-attributable adverse outcomes, including preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, and preterm birth, were lower in twin pregnancies compared to singleton pregnancies.
mod_finding: Obesity increased the risk of cesarean section in singleton pregnancies but not in twin pregnancies.
